8. External Club Supervisor – Role, Eligibility & Appointment
If a coach, parent, or school teacher is appointed as club manager or supervisor, the following conflicts arise:
Coach may select only "his" favorite players, ignore merit
Parent may favor their own child or create team politics
Teacher may prioritize their own school's students over others in a cluster
The principal may not have time; also, they may be biased toward their own school
8.2 The Solution – External, Neutral Club Supervisor
Each club (whether single-school or cluster) will have an external club supervisor who is:
Cannot be the same person as the head coach or any assistant coach
Cannot be a parent of any player in the club
Not a teacher from participating schools
For clusters, cannot be employed by any school in the cluster
No conflict of interest at school leadership level
To avoid favoritism toward MCD clubs
8.3 Who Can Be an External Club Supervisor?
The following individuals are eligible to be Club Supervisors:
MCD/DoE/Sports Authority of India retired staff
Empaneled list maintained by Khelo Tech
NCC / Scout & Guide officer (retired or active, with permission)
8.4 Who Is NOT Eligible (Conflict of Interest)
Head coach or assistant coach of the same club
Parent of any player in the club
Teacher or staff of any school in the club (for clusters)
Principal of any school in the club
8.5 Role & Responsibilities of External Club Supervisor
Ensure all player registrations are complete, age proofs uploaded
Verify player attendance independently (not relying only on the coach).
Resolve disputes between players, parents, or coaches within the club
Ensure coaches and players follow code of conduct
Report any issues to Zone Coordinator
Oversee collection and use of club funds (if any)
Ensure all coaches have background checks, report any concerns
Anonymous feedback from parents to be shared with MCD
8.6 How External Club Supervisors Are Appointed
Khelo Tech maintains a central empaneled list of eligible supervisors
Club applies for a supervisor via GMS (after club registration)
Khelo Tech assigns a supervisor from the empaneled list (randomized, zone-wise)
Supervisor is introduced to the club (virtual or in-person)
Supervisor signs a Code of Conduct and Conflict of Interest declaration
Supervisor receives GMS access (limited to view-only + reporting)

The MCD Mini League is a city-wide grassroots sports initiative dedicated to transforming the sporting landscape of Delhi through community participation, club development, athlete growth, and structured competition.

Designed to create sustainable sporting opportunities for children and young athletes, the league connects communities, clubs, coaches, volunteers, and institutions through a unified sports ecosystem that promotes participation, development, and excellence.

Through structured competitions, club-based training environments, athlete development programmes, and talent identification pathways, the MCD Mini League is building the foundation for the next generation of athletes while strengthening community engagement through sport.

The MCD Mini League is committed to making sports accessible, inclusive, and impactful across Delhi. By supporting clubs, athletes, coaches, and volunteers, the league is creating opportunities that extend far beyond competition.
Our focus is on participation, development, leadership, and community engagement, ensuring that every athlete has access to meaningful sporting experiences.

This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) establishes the standardized, technology-enabled process governing the registration, verification, approval, and onboarding of Clubs participating in the MCD Mini Football League (MMFL). It is issued to ensure that every Club is registered through a uniform, transparent, auditable, and legally defensible process.
To establish a single, government-endorsed pathway for Club formation and registration across Delhi-NCR.
To ensure standardization of eligibility, documentation, verification, and approval across all 12 MCD Zones.
To safeguard the core motive of the League -
- through accurate, fraud-resistant registration and age-verification protocols.
To enable a digital-first, paperless registration workflow through the Game Management System (GMS).
To establish clear roles, timelines, and escalation paths so that no application remains unresolved beyond the prescribed period.
To protect the safety and welfare of minor participants through Child Protection and Safeguarding compliance embedded in the registration process.

This SOP applies to the end-to-end lifecycle of Club registration - from issuance of the Government Notice through to a Club attaining 'Ready for League' status and fixture eligibility. It initially covers Football, U-9 and U-11 age categories, Boys' and Girls' teams, and is applicable uniformly to MCD Clubs and Non-MCD Clubs.

3.3 Eligibility Restrictions, Disqualifications and Conflict of Interest
A school may be affiliated with only one Club per sport in a given season; dual affiliation renders both applications void.
A Club found to have submitted fraudulent age, identity, or school-affiliation documents shall be disqualified for the season and referred to the Risk Management process (Section 17).
No coach, parent, teacher, or principal associated with a Club may simultaneously serve as its External Club Supervisor (see Section 8.4).
No current MCD employee may be appointed as External Club Supervisor of any Club, to avoid perceived favoritism toward MCD Clubs.
A Club under active suspension from a prior season may not re-register until the suspension period lapses and any outstanding fines are cleared.

Every Club must field four teams per sport — U-9 Boys, U-9 Girls, U-11 Boys, and U-11 Girls — with a minimum of 8 players per team (32 players minimum per Club per sport) for the inaugural season, and an ideal strength of 12–15 players per team (48–60 players per Club per sport) thereafter.

4.8 Club Dissolution, Mergers, Renaming, Ownership and Succession

Dissolution: A Club may be dissolved by mutual written consent of all constituent zones, submitted to the Zone Coordinator; players are released to re-register with another eligible Club within the current registration window.
Mergers: Two Clubs may merge only before the Player Registration deadline, subject to League Director approval and a revised Cluster Agreement.
Renaming: Any change of Club name after initial approval requires a fresh Zone Coordinator naming clearance.
Ownership: A Club's registration is held in trust for its constituent school(s); no individual may claim personal ownership of Club branding, GMS credentials, or player data.
Succession: On rotation of the Club Manager (annual, per the Cluster Agreement), GMS access and all Club records transfer formally to the incoming Manager with Zone Coordinator countersignature.

8.3 Refund, Late Fee, Cancellation and Transfer

Refund Policy: Full refund if a Club's application is rejected at Zone Coordinator or League Director verification through no fault of the applicant; no refund once a Club reaches 'Approved' status and player registration has commenced.
Late Fee: Applications submitted after the notified deadline attract a late fee as specified in the annual registration calendar (Section 14), subject to League Director discretion.
Cancellation Fee: A Club voluntarily withdrawing after payment but before approval forfeits 25% of the registration fee as a processing charge.
Transfer Fee: Fees paid are non-transferable between Clubs except in the case of an approved Club merger (Section 4.8).
Payment Modes: UPI, Net Banking, Credit/Debit Card, NEFT/RTGS, or Demand Draft (for institutions without digital payment access).
Invoice Generation: GMS auto-generates a GST-compliant invoice on successful payment.
GST Applicability: Applicable as per prevailing government norms for the registering entity type; corporate-sponsored Clubs must furnish GST details where applicable.
Receipt Generation: A digital receipt is issued instantly and stored in the Club's GMS document repository.
Financial Approvals: All fee waivers and refunds require League Director sign-off and are logged for audit (Section 16).

On successful clearance of all four verification layers, the League Director issues final Club approval within GMS, activating the Player Registration module. Approval may be granted in one of three forms:
Conditional Approval — granted where minor, non-blocking deficiencies remain (e.g., pending bank details), with a defined cure period.
Provisional Approval — granted ahead of full document verification to allow player registration to begin within tight seasonal timelines, subject to retrospective confirmation within 10 days.
Final Approval — granted once all layers of verification are complete and no deficiencies remain.

A rejected Club may file a written appeal to the League Director within 7 calendar days of rejection, accompanied by corrected or additional documentation. The League Director shall issue a decision within 10 calendar days of receipt of the appeal. The League Director's decision on appeal is final at the operational level, subject to further escalation per Section 2.4.
10.3 Approval Validity, Renewal, Suspension and Termination
Validity: Club approval is valid for the League season for which it is granted and does not automatically carry forward.
Renewal: Clubs must re-register each season; returning Clubs follow an expedited verification track where prior-season records show no compliance issues.
Suspension: A Club may be suspended mid-season for non-compliance per the consequence framework in Section 10.4 and Section 20.2, pending investigation.

Termination: A Club's registration may be terminated for serious or repeated violations (fraud, safeguarding breaches), with all matches forfeited and re-registration barred for a period determined by the League Director.

Disputes must be filed within 7 calendar days of the triggering decision and are adjudicated within 10 calendar days of filing. The Appeals Committee's decision is final at the operational level, subject to escalation per the Governance Framework (Section 2.4).

Q: Can a school join more than one Club? A: No — a school may be affiliated with only one Club per sport per season.
Q: What happens if a Club misses the document deadline? A: The application moves to 'Action Required' with a 5-day cure period, after which it lapses to 'Expired'.
Q: Who bears the cost of forming a Cluster? A: Constituent zones share the registration fee as agreed in the Cluster Agreement; Khelo Tech facilitation itself is free of charge.
Q: Can a coach also be the External Club Supervisor? A: No — this is an absolute conflict-of-interest restriction (Section 8.4).
Q: What if a player's age document is disputed? A: The case is escalated to the League Director, who may require a medical/age certificate from an authorized hospital (Section 9.2).
